newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt bourse seen watching U.S., volumes light.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt bourse seen watching U.S., volumes light.

text.p: German shares were expected to hover around current levels on Friday, but to keep a close watch on developments on Wall Street and more important data due out of the U.S.
But dealers said volumes would be light because of a public holiday in several German states.

The IBIS DAX, which measures all-day computer trade in 30 leading shares, was up 3.11 points, or 0.12 percent, at 2,667.83 in afternoon dealings, off earlier lows after Wall Street opened slightly firmer and U.S. Treasuries were encouraged by data showing higher-than-expected jobless claims.

Analysts at ABN-Amro expect an end to the current consolidation phase in the first week of November. But Societe Generale said the phase may continue for the next couple of weeks, with the DAX index hovering plus or minus 10 points around the 2,660 point level.
Dealers said SAP could continue to attract attention as analysts downgraded expectations for the company, following its profit warning last week.
SAP preference shares, which lost almost a quarter of their value last Wednesday, were down 5.90 marks, or almost three percent, at 199 marks in late IBIS trade.

Meanwhile, some dealers said carmaker Volkswagen had stepped into SAP's former position as market favourite, with several investment banks upgrading their forecasts for the company, following upbeat nine month results out last week.
VW shares rose 6.30 marks, or over one percent, to 604.30 marks in IBIS trade, after Merrill Lynch named the company as its Global Focus One stock.
The brokerage said it maintained its near-term buy rating and long-term accumulate rating on the carmaker.
